name: building-research-progression-visual
description: Visual check of the research tier-gate: Tier 1 Research Center placed, a direct Tier 2 attempt rejected, Tier 2 researched instantly (cost-only), an early Tier 3 attempt rejected by the conditions gate, then Tier 2 is built once researched — which overdraws this file's modest starting cash deeply negative (Finding #1's class: build has no funds guard) and, as a real consequence, Tier 3 research itself is then rejected for insufficient_funds and never completes. building-research-visual.json (higher starting cash) is the sibling file that carries the T1→T2→T3 progression through to a real Tier 3 build.

steps.description: Left unmarked: at this point the button is genuinely disabled (tier not yet researched / affordable, or the target id doesn't exist), so a real player could not click it either -- this step deliberately demonstrates the rejection command mode shows via the same disabled-button rule that gates the UI. Not converted to a click; the console command reproduces the same no-op the disabled button would.
Tier-2 (first upgrade) is cost-only — no duration, no conditions.

Rejected (conditions_not_met) — tier-3's own condition (tier-2 research completed) is not yet satisfied: tier-2 is only queued, not yet processed by a tick. Demonstrates the conditions gate before the flow below completes tier-2 and queues tier-3 successfully.

expect.note: rejected: tier 2 research is only queued, not yet completed

steps.description: Tier-2 is 0-duration — a single tick is enough to complete it.

expect.note: tiny ambient drain from the tick itself, separate from the research (paid in full at queue time) — decreased not equals per Finding #12

steps.description: Left unmarked: cash is already at or below this building's cost at this point in the scenario, so the Build panel's buy button is disabled (BuildMenu.ts: `btn.disabled = cash < def.constructionCost || locked`) and a real player could not click it -- but the console `build` command has no funds guard and drives cash negative anyway (Finding #1's class, previously only confirmed for `vehicle buy`; this generalizes it to plain `build` too). Found by the interaction channel: command mode passes this step silently by overdrawing, something no click can do.

expect.note: Finding #20: this succeeds (tier 2 IS researched) but the $60,000 cost drives cash deeply negative from this file's modest 50,000 starting cash — a real consequence of Finding #1's class that cascades into the next step's rejection

steps.description: Finding #20: does NOT succeed despite tier-3's condition (tier-2 research completed) being satisfied — the prior step's overdraw (Finding #1's class) leaves cash too negative to afford this task's $12,000 cost, so it is rejected for insufficient_funds instead. The scenario's original description claimed this succeeds and tier 3 unlocks over the following ticks; a real dump shows neither happens. building-research-visual.json (higher starting cash) is the sibling file where this task genuinely queues and completes.

expect.note: rejected: insufficient_funds — tier 3 research never actually queues in this file

steps.description: Finding #20: "No research queued" — the prior step's queue attempt was rejected (insufficient_funds), so there is nothing here to progress despite the tier-3 gate condition being satisfied.
Finding #20: still "No research queued" — these ticks have nothing to advance since tier-3 research was never queued.
Finding #20: still "No research queued" at the 50-tick mark this file's original description claimed tier-3 research would complete at — it was never queued in the first place.

Left unmarked: at this point the button is genuinely disabled (tier not yet researched), so a real player could not click it either -- this step deliberately demonstrates the rejection command mode shows via the same disabled-button rule that gates the UI. Not converted to a click; the console command reproduces the same no-op the disabled button would. Finding #20: rejected for the same reason as the tier-2 direct attempt earlier in this file (tier 3 was never researched, since its research queue attempt failed for insufficient_funds, not because "the target id doesn't exist" as the generic boilerplate elsewhere in this file would suggest).

expect.note: rejected: tier 3 not researched — building-count stays at 2, confirming tier 3 was never actually reached in this file
